name: Vernon Lee
bio: Aesthetician, critic, novelist and writer of supernatural tales, born Violet Paget at Chateau St Leonard near Boulogne-sur-Mer on 14 October 1856 and resident for most of her life in Italy, latterly at Il Palmerino, Maiano. She adopted the androgynous pen name "Vernon Lee" in the late 1870s and came to public notice in 1880 with Studies of the Eighteenth Century in Italy. Two long attachments to women structure her life as the Y90s biography records it: the poet Mary Robinson (1857-1944), from 1880 until Robinson's marriage in 1887, and Clementina "Kit" Anstruther-Thomson (1857-1921), her companion and co-author from 1887 to 1900. She met Wilde in London in 1881 at the Robinsons', and appears in the Complete Letters only in the editors' apparatus, which quotes her own letters describing him; there is no correspondence between them in the volume. Amy Levy fell in love with her at Florence in 1886. Lee died at Il Palmerino on 13 February 1935.
bio_note: Birth and death dates and places, the pen-name adoption, and both attachments from Patricia Pulham's Y90s biography of Vernon Lee (2018/2019). Dates corroborated by the editors' footnote in Wilde's Complete Letters (2000), p. 229, read at the rendered page image, which identifies "Violet Paget (1856-1935), who lived mostly in Italy and published many books under the name Vernon Lee".
